steps.label: Alice holds |ψ⟩ = 0.6|0⟩ + 0.8|1⟩ — unknown to her
steps.sub: If she already knew it, she could just tell Bob the amplitudes

steps.label: Alice and Bob each hold half of a Bell pair |Φ+⟩
Three qubits total
steps.sub: Alice's unknown qubit, Alice's half of the pair, Bob's half

eyebrow: Verified: Alice's outcome determines Bob's fix
code:
Alice's Bell-basis outcome: each of 4, exactly P = 0.25

outcome  Bob's qubit (raw)  correction  result
Phi+     (0.6,  0.8)        I          (0.6, 0.8)
Phi-     (0.6, -0.8)        Z          (0.6, 0.8)
Psi+     (0.8,  0.6)        X          (0.6, 0.8)
Psi-     (-0.8, 0.6)        X then Z   (0.6, 0.8)
caption: In every one of the four cases, the matching correction recovers exactly the original |ψ⟩ — no approximation.

steps.label: Her outcome is 2 classical bits — sent over an ordinary channel
steps.sub: A phone call, email, radio signal, anything

steps.label: Without that message, Bob can't pick the correction
steps.sub: His qubit alone can't be used to extract |ψ⟩

steps.label: The classical message travels at or below light speed
Alice's Bell measurement collapses her original qubit
steps.sub: After the protocol, only Bob has |ψ⟩ — Alice has nothing

steps.label: Exactly one copy exists at every point in time
It moves the state, destroying the original as it goes
steps.sub: Costs: 1 Bell pair, 1 Bell measurement, 2 classical bits

subtitle: Running the resource trade in reverse: 2 classical bits from 1 transmitted qubit.
